summary: Hotpatch off-ramp for optimizer policies and KV-eviction causing tenant tail latency
description:
Issue summary:
BlueHarbor reported a 95th/99th percentile latency spike for their tenant after we enabled a live optimizer profile that toggles aggressive KV prefetch and async batching. Impact:
- Several customer endpoints experienced long tail latency (95p -> 2.1s, 99p -> 4.3s) and intermittent streaming disconnects for multi-turn chat flows.
- Customer SLA-sensitive workflows (billing reconciliation) affected.
Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dh-prod-12a (us-east)
- Optimizer flags: aggressive_kv_prefetch=true, async_batching=on, quant_profile=fp16-mix
- Traffic split: 10% live rollout to BlueHarbor tenant only
Steps to reproduce:
1) Send multi-turn chat requests with long contexts (~1.2k tokens) to BlueHarbor tenant route
2) Observe 95p/99p token latency and streaming stalls in traces
Observed behavior:
- Increased tail token generation time after KV eviction cycles; backend traces show high scheduler queueing on serving-runtime and repeated KV eviction/rehydration events for tenant cache entries.
Expected behavior:
- Stable 95p/99p latency within historical baseline (~350ms/600ms) after optimizer changes for a controlled 10% rollout.
Logs / metrics collected:
- Traces: link to sampling traces in Console (trace IDs attached in comments)
- Dashboards: per-tenant latency chart spike (attached screenshot in support UI)
Previous attempts:
- Temporarily reduced rollout from 10% -> 2% (no immediate improvement)
- Applied soft throttle on async_batching flag for other tenants (BlueHarbor still impacted)
Request / ask:
- We need an actionable hotpatch off-ramp guidance to safely pull aggressive_kv_prefetch and async_batching for only BlueHarbor tenant with minimal blips to live traffic and a recommended sequence of steps (drain, snapshot restore, per-tenant gating) and checks to confirm safe recovery.
investigation_notes: 03-12 09:20: Initial triage: KPIs show correlated KV eviction counts spiked at rollout time for dh-prod-12a.
03-12 10:02: Trace samples show repeated cache-miss thrash: eviction->rehydrate cycles for tenant-specific prefix entries.
03-12 11:15: Hypothesis: aggressive_kv_prefetch combined with async_batching changes increased memory churn on per-GPU KV structures, triggering eviction thrash under tenant's long-context workload.
03-12 12:05: Verified other tenants in same pool with shorter context lengths did not exhibit same tail behavior; suggests workload interaction with optimizer profile.
03-12 13:40: Attempted traffic reduction; tail latency persisted indicating need for direct off-ramp rather than traffic throttling alone.

resolution: In progress: staging-validated hotpatch runbook prepared. Next actions: execute per-tenant snapshot restore and toggle aggressive_kv_prefetch in production for BlueHarbor during 09:30 window; monitor 95p/99p for 30m and, if stable, follow with async_batching disable. Post-action follow-up will capture telemetry and recommend permanent profile adjustments or a slower staged rollout.
